name: Central bank stress
value: Fed Dec rise priced ~89%; BoE leans to rise
summary: Markets price a December Fed rise at about 89% after hot inflation; BoE officials also signal a further rise
state: After October CPI beat forecasts, Fed Governor Waller said on 10 Nov he would back a December rise and a half-point move should be considered; CME FedWatch showed about an 89% chance of a quarter-point rise and 11% of a half-point (MPA, 11 Nov). Bank of England Deputy Governor Lombardelli said on 10 Nov there is likely a case for a further rise in the near term (Pound Sterling Live). Central banks face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency inter-meeting move was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Rate rises by several major central banks at once tend to lift mortgage and loan costs and can unsettle bond and currency markets. Households on variable-rate or soon-to-renew borrowing are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma, with inflation rising as Fed and BoE signal hikes; no emergency move (Alert)

sources.title: MPA — Fed rate hike odds hit 100% as Waller floats bigger December move
Pound Sterling Live — Bank of England's Lombardelli Says December Rate Rise is in Play

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
